<reason>Both sides were sharp and the clash narrowed properly. CON's best move was the counter-model of data-matched, community- and direct-certification targeting, which captured most of PRO's dignity/paperwork benefits while preserving the opportunity-cost story. But PRO turned that model against CON twice and profitably: first by showing that building-level free meals are themselves universalism (leaving only the question of unit), then by pressing the zip-code hole and the population data matching cannot see (just-above-SNAP, eligible-but-unenrolled, undocumented-avoidant). PRO's Pressure Questions were the most productive round in the debate: Q1 extracted CON's explicit concession that a residual gap is "a real design problem," and Q2 exposed that CON's crowd-out claim rests on an unstated assumption of redirection. CON's answer that anti-hunger money sits in statutory poverty-tied line items was honest but partly self-defeating: if the pot is statutorily earmarked by poverty data, savings from not feeding middle-income kids do not automatically flow to backpack or breakfast programs, so the central "diluted pot" premise stayed under-grounded. CON also never engaged PRO's administrative-cost point (verification, lunch debt, tiered cashier accounts), which quietly narrowed the alleged savings. CON's recovery — "fix the small leak, don't flood the boat," plus the burden challenge that PRO never shows universality closes the gap faster than fixing it directly — was genuinely strong and kept this competitive, and PRO's answer (designing around human failure rather than assuming it away, plus the error-asymmetry frame) was adequate rather than overwhelming. PRO's asymmetry weighing — an uncounted hungry child versus a wealthy family recovering some of its own taxes — was the clearest decision rule offered and survived the exchange. Clear but competitive edge to PRO.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Rebuttal 1 [A2.1]-[A2.4], recasting CON's community-eligibility fix as universalism-within-a-building and then puncturing it with the poor child in the affluent district. That forced CON onto individual data matching, which PRO's Q1 then exposed as leaky, extracting CON's "remaining sliver is a real design problem" concession that PRO exploited in closing.</best_rebuttal>
